points.description: States that array elements can be accessed directly (random access / by index, constant time), rather than needing to be reached by traversal.
points.partial_credit: Half or more if vague, e.g. says arrays are faster or easier to access without mentioning direct/index access; or states direct access with a minor error.

points.description: Contrasts with linked lists, which require iterative traversal (going through nodes one by one) to reach an element.
points.partial_credit: Half if only says linked lists are slower to access without mentioning traversal.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that array elements are accessed directly (by index/random access), in any wording; the linked-list contrast earns the last mark. Part marks for vague claims like 'arrays are faster to access' without direct or index access. No marks for unrelated advantages such as memory use or insertion, or if the answer claims linked lists have the direct access.
